name: Vecorin
manufacturer: Unlicensed — attributed to the Gray Zone chemist collective known as the Apostles
description: A fast-acting neuromuscular blocking agent derived from modified dendrotoxin analogs, engineered to spare respiratory function at standard doses — the target is fully paralyzed but breathing and conscious. Onset is 8-15 seconds via injection. Used by kidnapping crews, corpo extraction teams, and black-bag operators who need a compliant, aware subject.
effects: complete voluntary motor paralysis within 15 seconds
respiratory muscles spared at doses under 3mL
side_effects: extreme psychological trauma from conscious paralysis
autonomic dysregulation causing uncontrolled tear production and salivation
doses above 3.5mL cross into respiratory paralysis — lethal without ventilator support
prolonged use causes permanent neuromuscular junction degradation
subjects with chrome limbs experience partial override — augmented limbs may twitch or spasm unpredictably
duration: 45-90 minutes per dose; fully reversible with Vecorin-R antagonist
cultural_context: Standard equipment for the Gray Zone kidnapping rings and corpo black-bag squads alike — the economics are different but the application is identical. The Apostles are known for consistent dosing quality, which is why even Tier 3 operators buy down to the Gray Zone rather than risk a batch that stops breathing. The phrase 'gone to Marble' in the Gray Zone slang means someone's been taken.
story_hooks: A kidnapping victim, fully paralyzed and aware, memorizes every detail of the safe house they're held in. When they're eventually released, they become the most dangerous witness anyone has ever created.
A corpo extraction team uses Vecorin on the wrong target — a Tier 5 executive's body double. The real target is now alerted and the team is holding someone who will be missed immediately.
The Apostles' latest batch has a contamination issue — the respiratory threshold has dropped to 2mL. Bodies are turning up that were supposed to be live deliveries.
